PCG.thesis_one_line: California power and gas utility growing earnings about 8% a year, priced cheaply because one big wildfire could wreck it.
kill_criteria: A wildfire attributed to PG&E equipment with estimated claims above $1.0B (the Wildfire Fund threshold per 10-Q) in any coverage year, or any Cal Fire report naming Utility equipment for a fire exceeding 100,000 acres.
Annual non-GAAP core EPS guidance cut below the low end of the prior range in any release (2026 range $1.64-$1.66), or 2027 guidance implying less than 7% growth.
Any announced PG&E Corporation common equity issuance before 2030 (contradicts the 10-Q statement) or dilution above 5% of diluted shares.
Any downgrade of the Utility to below its current unsecured rating by the agency that rates it below investment grade, or loss of investment grade at the other agencies.
CPUC decision disallowing more than $500M of the $1.59B Kincade/Dixie AB 1054 cost-recovery application (filed 14 Nov 2025).
key_adverse_facts: Consolidated debt about $64.2B (carrying, 30 Jun 2026) against equity $33.9B; TTM free cash flow about -$4.3B
Utility unsecured rating below investment grade at one agency (10-Q 0001004980-26-000048)
Dixie fire: about 190 complaints for at least 9,062 plaintiffs; $1.59B Kincade/Dixie cost-recovery application pending, $674M drawn from Wildfire Fund
Wildfire Fund asset being amortised faster ($126M expense in Q2 2026 vs $109M)
2027-2030 at-least-9% EPS growth last stated in the Q3 2025 release, not repeated in 2026 releases opened
data_conflicts: d4 implied shares 3.0B / market cap $37.0B vs 10-Q 2,202M basic, 2,285M diluted shares
d4 free cash flow -$6.15B vs filing-derived TTM about -$4.3B
PCG.confidence_in_thesis: low-to-med: earnings path is well guided, but the wildfire tail cannot be bounded from filings

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for PCG. Price at $12.34 implies about 4-6% core EPS growth from $1.65, but from a GAAP-adjusted $1.43 (recurring non-core costs about $0.22 a year) it implies about 5.6-7.6% versus my 7% base and management's at-least-9% target (Oct 2025). Restated below -> in line by DVH5, 2026-10-06; verdict unchanged.

PCG.scenario_basis: Start core EPS $1.65 (2026 guide midpoint), EPS growth 0/7/10%, exit P/E 5.5/8.5/11x, dividend $0.20 growing 5%; from $12.34; excludes a separate catastrophic-fire scenario.

AWK.thesis_one_line: Largest US water utility with steady 7-9% earnings growth, but the price already reflects that and a merger is pending.
kill_criteria: 2026 adjusted EPS guidance cut below $6.02, or H2 2026 adjusted EPS growth below 5% year on year.
Essential Utilities merger terminated, or any final PUC order adding conditions that the company calls a "Burdensome Effect", or closing slipping past 30 Jun 2027.
Long-term EPS/dividend growth target lowered below 7% (current 7-9%).
Consolidated net debt / EBITDA above 6.0x or either Moody's/S&P downgrade of American Water Capital Corp. senior notes.
Any adverse final judgment over $200M in the Chattanooga or other class actions (10-Q legal note).
key_adverse_facts: Consolidated net debt about $15.8B; TTM free cash flow about -$1.0B; equity forward shares (4.69M) still to settle
Essential Utilities all-stock merger (0.305 AWK share per Essential share) not yet approved in Pennsylvania; non-unanimous settlement filed 15 Sep 2026
H1 2026 adjusted EPS growth only 4.4% versus 7.6% needed for guidance midpoint
New $500M 5.550% notes due 2033 priced 14 Sep 2026, showing higher funding costs
data_conflicts: d4 free cash flow -$1.79B vs filing-derived TTM about -$1.0B
AWK.confidence_in_thesis: med: business quality is high and guidance reliable; limited margin of safety at 21.6x

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for AWK. Price implies about 5.3% EPS growth (4.4-6.3% across assumptions) against a 7% base; the gap is small and merger dilution is not in guidance.

AWK.scenario_basis: Start adjusted EPS $6.07 (2026 guide midpoint), EPS growth 4/7/9%, exit P/E 16/20/23x, dividend $3.58 growing 8%; from $130.91.

FFIV.thesis_one_line: Sells and secures the traffic layer of big company applications; excellent cash flow, but price assumes growth a hardware upgrade cycle may not sustain.
kill_criteria: Fiscal-year guidance cut: any release lowering FY non-GAAP EPS or revenue growth below the prior range (current FY26 range $17.21-$17.33, revenue +9% to +10%).
Product revenue growth below 5% year on year in two consecutive quarters (Q3 FY26 +19%).
Non-GAAP operating margin below 33% in any quarter (Q3 FY26 35.0%).
A quantified loss or regulatory action from the Cyber Incident above $100M, or a customer-notified BIG-IP vulnerability causing named enterprise churn disclosed in a 10-Q/8-K.
Inventory above $200M without corresponding product revenue growth above 15%, or consolidated cash below $1.0B.
key_adverse_facts: October 2025 security incident with long-term persistent access and exfiltrated files; securities class action (Smith v. F5) and two derivative suits
Systems revenue +32% in Q3 FY26 is cycle-driven; inventory $126.9M vs $77.2M at 30 Sep 2025
Stock-based compensation about 7.6% of revenue; non-GAAP EPS excludes it; Q3 tax rate 8%
Software revenue growth lumpy: -8% Q1, +17% Q2, +7% Q3 FY26
data_conflicts: d4 free cash flow $717M vs filing-derived TTM about $970M (OCF $1,049M less capex about $80M)
d4/Yahoo total debt $252M is operating lease liabilities; no borrowings per 10-Q
FFIV.confidence_in_thesis: med: execution and guidance record strong; valuation leaves little margin

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for FFIV. Price implies about 14% annual growth in SBC-adjusted FCF per share (about 10.7% on non-GAAP EPS) versus my 8% base.

FFIV.scenario_basis: Start FY26 non-GAAP EPS $17.27 (guide midpoint), EPS growth 0/8/13%, exit P/E 16/22/26x, no dividend; from $443.06.
